checks.scope: Definition prose is separated from planning history and runtime constraints.
checks.observable: Ask whether the clause describes current behavior or requires remembering an alternative design.
checks.consistency: Matches DP-17 without banning every English negation.
checks.exceptions: Runtime prohibitions, schema operators, catalog examples, and validation errors are explicitly retained.
checks.fix: Rewrite around the current behavior while preserving live constraints.
checks.expression: The edit-when-old-way-is-forgotten signal makes the stylistic goal operational.

rationale: 'The workflow now avoids the old manual path' differs from a current invariant such as 'Secrets stay out of artifacts'.

checks.scope: I/O descriptions naming workflow-internal producers or consumers are the subject.
checks.observable: Inspect the named/link target and whether it identifies a particular workflow position.
checks.consistency: Consistent with DP-37; AP-125 adds the broader technique-link form.
checks.exceptions: Intrinsic/external origins and resource links describing shape remain useful contract facts.
checks.fix: State meaning, shape, and allowed values without the caller's topology.
checks.expression: The boundary between a value's nature and one caller's source is well illustrated.

rationale: 'Findings from the assessment activity' couples a contract; 'Findings with severity and source evidence' defines the value.

checks.scope: Literal artifact references and path-flavored ids are both named.
checks.observable: Compare the Protocol reference with declared I/O and artifact metadata.
checks.consistency: The literal-file case duplicates AP-44; identifier shape is also owned by AP-66.
checks.exceptions: Artifact declaration literals and resource-template nouns are expressly allowed.
checks.fix: Use the declared designator and preserve filename metadata at its declaration.
checks.expression: Separating reference syntax from id shape would give each invariant one home.

rationale: The checks are observable; consolidate duplicated ownership rather than label the overlap a contradiction.

checks.scope: Concrete artifact filenames inside Protocol are a precise target.
checks.observable: A literal filename can be compared directly with its declared artifact/input id.
checks.consistency: The same case and remedy appear in AP-43; AP-130 owns the declaration grammar.
checks.exceptions: Canonical designators are excluded and opaque arrays have their own check.
checks.fix: Move the filename to the declaration and use the identifier in work instructions.
checks.expression: Keep one Protocol-filename entry and point to the filename grammar owner.

rationale: The individual rule is usable, but one construct need not yield both AP-43 and AP-44 findings.

checks.scope: An opaque array replacing distinct semantic artifact inputs is the target.
checks.observable: Show that Protocol must recover file identities the input contract does not name.
checks.consistency: Fits AP-43/AP-44's declaration ownership without banning every collection.
checks.exceptions: A single named artifact is explicit; a meaningful structured collection does not satisfy the opaque/forced-filename Detect.
checks.fix: Give fixed semantic artifact roles their own declared inputs.
checks.expression: The forced-Protocol-filenames condition keeps the rule narrower than a ban on path arrays by name alone.

rationale: An unordered list of specification/review paths that the procedure must identify by filename differs from a declared collection whose entries already carry semantic roles.

checks.scope: Ordinary resources naming host callers, destinations, or binding topology are explicit.
checks.observable: Delete the host narrative and verify that template/vocabulary/guide use remains complete.
checks.consistency: The prompt-domain exception accommodates resources whose subject is running the engine.
checks.exceptions: Creation-guide artifact names, template filenames, shape headings, and appropriate resource references are retained.
checks.fix: Move actual orchestration into its owning activity or technique and preserve usable fill material.
checks.expression: Examples are numerous but the host-coupling predicate and exceptions provide a coherent decision.

rationale: 'Used by activity X at gate Y' is incidental to a general template; a creation guide's subject filename is not that incidental backlink.

checks.scope: Immediate textual repetition before a same-name hyperlink is precisely scoped.
checks.observable: Normalize case, hyphen, and underscore and compare the two labels.
checks.consistency: No broader reference or contract rule requires the redundant wrapper.
checks.exceptions: A distinct preceding role label is explicitly preserved.
checks.fix: A single hyperlink preserves both the name and navigation.
checks.expression: The concrete text pattern and normalization rule are sufficient.

rationale: deep_scan followed by a same-name parenthetical link is redundant; a role word followed by a different resource id is informative.

checks.scope: References to declared outputs are the scope, not all descriptive nouns.
checks.observable: Named output slots make ambiguity testable, but the current noun list treats unique anaphora as vague.
checks.consistency: General reference entries allow same-step anaphora; output-specific strictness could be intentional.
checks.exceptions: Existing designators and non-output prose are excluded; unique anchored anaphora is unstated.
checks.fix: Substitute the id when needed to identify the output; decide whether machine processing needs every repetition.
checks.expression: Distinguish ambiguity from a stricter formatting requirement.

rationale: State a consistent reference policy; no contradiction is claimed solely from a narrower style rule.
